messages:
sasha: throwing this out there: propose a 'tier graceband' feature for pricing transitions. idea = when usage crosses a tier boundary, don't flip immediately. instead enter a graceband period where we hold tier for N days and only promote/demote if sustained. avoids churn and angry customers.

rahul: love the idea. couple constraints: 1) how do we represent this in contracts (effective date / freeze clauses)? 2) how do add-ons/kickins behave during the band?

jyoti: product angle: propose defaults = 10-day graceband + optional 'contractual hold' for enterprise customers (requires explicit consent in contract). during graceband: runtime throttles and quota enforcement unchanged; only billing tier updates are deferred. add-on triggers still record, but we mark them as 'in-band' and reconcile after band ends.

emily-sales: Sales POV: enterprise will want a 'contractual hold' unlock that prevents automatic demotion/promotion without written approval. also need a clear migration simulation so AE can show impact for renewal negotiations.

legal-bot: Heads-up: any change that affects billing cadence or tiering needs TOS addendum and 45-day notice. contractual hold entries must be auditable and stored as part of contract metadata.

billing-bot: Note: reconcile rules must produce deterministic invoice lines. If graceband defers a promotion and later it becomes permanent, we either bill retroactively (not preferred) or bill forward from detection date. Need decision.

sasha: prefer forward-only billing to avoid retroactive invoices. if band ends and tier up, bill at next invoice at new tier; if sustained over prior period we could offer an optional retrospective credit for fairness (configurable per contract).

rahul: engineering implications: state machine per-customer storing: current_tier, band_state (enter_ts, expiry_ts, candidate_tier), add-on events flagged with candidate_tier. APIs: `POST /v1/customers/{id}/tier-band` to set overrides, `GET /v1/customers/{id}/tier-forecast?days=30` for Console projection. metric: `customer_tier_band_state`. estimated 2-3 sprints core + 1 sprint console + 1 sprint billing reconciliation work.

jyoti: launch criteria (compact): 1) RFC with contract language snippets; 2) Console forecast widget + toggle per-customer; 3) Billing replay tool with 12mo dataset + deterministic invoice outcomes; 4) Legal signoff + TOS addendum text; 5) Pilot: 2 hosted customers (SMB + midmarket) and 1 enterprise contractual-hold pilot; 6) Run disaster tests ensuring no effect on quota enforcement.

emily-sales: add to criteria: sales-facing one-pager, sample renewal clause, and a simulator spreadsheet AEs can use. also request an opt-in flag for pilots exposed in Contract playbook.

rahul: technical note: for retro-impact analysis we'll need a backfill replay job that can simulate both retro-billing and forward-only semantics to compare. also watch out for race conditions when customers change plan mid-band.

sasha: good point. let's require in launch checklist a 'mid-band switch policy' that spells out allowed changes and credits behavior.

legal-bot: also require audit logs for any manual overrides + signed opt-ins. I'll draft TOS addendum language.

billing-bot: I'll prototype reconciliation logic and provide sample invoice diff for the pilot customers once we have historical data.

jyoti: next steps: Sasha to write RFC and include simulation plan. Rahul to prototype API + metric names. Emily to surface pilot candidates and prep sales materials. Legal to draft addendum. Target milestone: include in next roadmap sync as candidate Q4 initiative. label: `pr/graceband-tier-v1`.

sasha: thanks all — I'll post a short RFC by EOD with mockups and the proposed defaults. ping me if you want to join pilot list. :sparkles:
